Data & methods

Where the data come from

NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 combines land and ocean observations on a 2° grid with 1,200 km smoothing. Temperature anomalies use NASA’s 1951–1980 baseline. Grid values describe a broad area, so a city label is a shortcut to its grid cell.

GPCP v2.3 satellite and gauge precipitation is provided by NOAA PSL on a 2.5° grid. Each cell’s precipitation anomaly is the change in mean daily precipitation relative to its own 1991–2020 average.

From months to years

Each annual value is a mean of 12 monthly values weighted by calendar days. A cell-year with a missing month is shown in gray. The color scale stays fixed while the timeline moves. Values outside the legend endpoints use the endpoint colors.

How trends are tested

The trend is the least squares slope across 30 consecutive annual values, expressed per decade. The confidence interval and two-sided p-value use a Newey–West standard error with three annual lags and an approximate normal reference distribution. The map colors represent slope magnitude. Each significance test applies to a single cell, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. The interval describes regression uncertainty and excludes uncertainty in the input dataset.
